item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 221136
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Thu Oct 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located several hundred miles south-southwest of
Acapulco, Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, a few hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll
late this weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the
system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Vance are issued under WMO
header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/advisories on Tropical Storm Vance are issued under WMO
header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 221446
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 AM CST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
...VANCE GETTING STRONGER WELL SOUTH OF MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...9.7N 101.0W
ABOUT 505 MI...810 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 680 MI...1095 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was 
re-positioned to near latitude 9.7 North, longitude 101.0 
West. Vance is moving toward the northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h), and 
a slow northwest to north-northwest motion is expected for the next 
few days.  
 
Satellite imagery indicate that the maximum sustained winds have 
increased to near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.  Vance is 
forecast to become a hurricane tonight and could become a major 
hurricane by the weekend.  
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 221448
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 AM CST Thu Oct 22 2026

Satellite imagery indicates that Vance is becoming better 
organized.  A central dense overcast has formed near the center, 
with apparently a low-level center re-formation to the east 
based on the latest microwave data. Objective and subjective 
Dvorak estimates are rising, and the latest estimates are between 
44-53 kt.  The initial intensity is set to 50 kt as a blend of the 
data.  

With the center re-formation, the initial motion is uncertain but 
is estimated to be northwest at about 3 kt.  There has been a 
substantial change in the guidance overnight, with the models 
showing a mid-level ridge over Mexico weakening faster than 
yesterday.  This pattern would allow the storm to move more to the 
northwest or north-northwest during the next several days.  The new 
forecast is shifted well to the northeast, near a blend of the 
latest GFS/ECMWF models. I will note that the Google DeepMind and 
HCCA aids are over a degree east of my new forecast by 96h, but 
continuity precludes a larger change at this time.  
 
The environment appears generally conducive for steady-to-rapid 
intensification during the next couple of days, with low shear, warm 
waters and plenty of mid-level moisture.  The forecast is about the 
same as the last one through 48 hours.  However, the new eastward 
track shift would bring Vance over the cold wake left by the gaggle 
of eastern Pacific hurricanes south of Mexico during the past few 
weeks, which could limit strengthening beyond 2 days.  Additionally, 
vertical wind shear is expected to increase early next week.    
Thus, the timing of the peak intensity has been adjusted to 
Saturday, and the long-range intensities have been reduced.  If 
farther east track shifts are required, the intensity forecast 
would likely have to be reduced as well for early next week since 
it would more squarely more over the cold wakes left behind the 
earlier hurricanes.
